newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY-BROSNIHAN WINS FIRST SPRINGBOK CAP.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY-BROSNIHAN WINS FIRST SPRINGBOK CAP.

text.p: Gauteng Lions flanker Warren Brosnihan will be the one new cap in the South African team to play Australia in a Tri-Nations Series test in Pretoria on Saturday.
Brosnihan, 25, replaces Ruben Kruger, who broke his ankle in the test defeat by New Zealand in Auckland last week.

The only other change to the side sees Free State flanker Johan Erasmus promoted from the bench to replace suspended Andre Venter, who was sent off against the All Blacks for stamping on Sean Fitzpatrick.
Uncapped Griqualand West utility back Franco Smith replaces Joe Gillingham on the bench. Springbok coach Carel du Plessis said Smith had been promoted to cover the flyhalf berth.
Ironically Smith, who went on last season's Springbok tour to Argentina, France and Wales, but failed to secure a test place, is currently playing at inside centre for his province.

Du Plessis has given a vote of confidence to fullback Russell Bennett and centre Percy Montgomery despite national condemnation. Bennett is keeping Andre Joubert, who is fit again, out of the side, while Montgomery could not even command a place in the Western Province team which played Gauteng Lions in a Currie Cup match on Sunday.
The Springboks will meet in Johannesburg on Monday and train there during the week. Australia have opted to stay in Durban ahead of the test in an attempt to neutralise the effects of altitude.
But the match is of little significance with New Zealand having wrapped up the title in Dunedin on Saturday.

South Africa: 15-Russell Bennett, 14-James Small, 13-Percy Montgomery, 12-Henry Honiball, 11-Andre Snyman, 10-Jannie de Beer, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen, 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Johan Erasmus, 6-Warren Brosnihan, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-Krynauw Otto, -Marius Hurter, 2-James Dalton, 1-Os du Randt.
Reserves: Pieter Rossouw, Franco Smith, Werner Swanepoel, Fritz van Heerden, Dawie Theron, Naka Drotske.
